practicals.label: Activity 1.01
practicals.bookText:
Classroom Discussion, Brainstorming, and System Mapping
Objective: To introduce the concept of systems and understand how different components interact within a system.
Required Material: Poster boards, markers, sticky notes, chart paper, drawing tools.
Activity Type: Group
Activity Tasks Detail: Start with a discussion where the teacher introduces the concept of systems using examples like cars and schools. Students will contribute their examples and ideas. Next perform, a brainstorming session, where students will work in groups to identify and list the systems they interact with daily. They will then create a system map on poster boards, labeling the components and their interactions. Finally, during a gallery walk, each group will present their system map, followed by a feedback session where the teacher provides feedback and answers questions.
Output: Each group will produce a system map poster illustrating their chosen system, and students will enhance their presentation and explanation skills.
procedure: The teacher introduces the concept of systems using examples like cars and schools.
Contribute examples and ideas during the discussion.
Work in groups to identify and list the systems you interact with daily.
Choose a system and create a system map on a poster board, labeling its components and their interactions.
During a gallery walk, present your group’s system map.
Take part in the feedback session; listen to the teacher’s feedback and ask or answer questions.
practicals.aim: To understand systems and how different components interact within a system by creating and presenting a system map.

viva.question: What is a system?
viva.answer: A system is a set of interacting components that work together.

viva.question: Name one example of a system.
viva.answer: A school is an example of a system.

viva.question: What does a system map show?
viva.answer: It shows a system’s components and the interactions between them.

viva.question: Why are interactions included in a system map?
viva.answer: They show how the components affect or connect with one another.

viva.question: What is a gallery walk?
viva.answer: It is an activity in which groups view and present their work to one another.

practicals.diagram: Draw a system map of the group’s chosen system on a poster board; label the system, each component, and the arrows showing interactions between components.
practicals.title: System Mapping
precautions: Make sure each component in the map is clearly labelled.
Use arrows clearly to show interactions between components.
Keep the poster layout neat and easy to read.
Listen respectfully to other groups during presentations and feedback.
practicals.result: The group produced and presented a system map showing the components of its chosen system and their interactions.

practicals.label: Activity 1.02
practicals.bookText:
Design a Simple System
Objective: To apply the principles of system design and understand the process of creating a functional system.
Required Material: Computers or tablets with diagramming software (e.g., Lucidchart), paper, pencils, markers.
Activity Type: Pair
Activity Tasks Detail: Begin with an introduction where the teacher presents an example of a simple system. Students will then work in pairs to define the objective of their chosen system, list its components, describe their interactions, and outline the system's environment. The pairs will use diagramming software to create a system prototype or diagram. Finally, they will present their designs to the class in a review and feedback session.
Output: Each pair will produce a system prototype or diagram and receive feedback to refine their design ideas.
procedure: Listen to the teacher’s introduction and example of a simple system.
Work in pairs and choose a system to design.
Define the objective of the chosen system.
List the system’s components.
Describe how the components interact.
Outline the system’s environment.
Use diagramming software to create a system prototype or diagram.
Present the design to the class and take part in the review and feedback session.
Use the feedback to refine the design.
practicals.aim: To apply the principles of system design by defining a system’s objective, components, interactions and environment, and creating a prototype or diagram.

viva.question: What is a system?
viva.answer: A set of interacting components working together to achieve an objective.

viva.question: What is the objective of a system?
viva.answer: The goal or purpose the system is designed to achieve.

viva.question: What are system components?
viva.answer: The parts that make up a system.

viva.question: What do interactions describe?
viva.answer: How the components of a system relate to or work with one another.

viva.question: What is a system’s environment?
viva.answer: The surroundings and external factors that can affect or interact with the system.

viva.question: Why is feedback useful when designing a system?
viva.answer: It helps identify improvements and refine the design.

apparatus: Computer or tablet with diagramming software
practicals.diagram: Draw a system diagram and label the system name, objective, components, interactions between components, and environment.
practicals.title: Designing a Simple System
precautions: Define the system’s objective clearly before drawing the diagram.
Include the main components needed to achieve the objective.
Show interactions between components clearly and accurately.
Label the system and its environment so the diagram is easy to understand.
Use the computer or tablet carefully and save the work.
practicals.result: A system prototype or diagram was created showing its objective, components, interactions and environment. Feedback was used to refine the design.

practicals.label: Activity 1.03
practicals.bookText:
Interactive Simulation
The purpose of this activity is with the aim of understanding how variability affects the system of interest.
Materials Needed: Computers or tablets with internet access and online simulation tools (like an ecosystem simulator).
Activity Tasks Detail: Individual or Group Assignments The teacher will begin by explaining what system dynamics entail as well as provide an overview on how the simulation will be implemented. Students will then work with the simulation tool, manipulating different variables and analyzing how the system reacts. Using an S-curve to review their results, the students will be reflecting on how changes impact the entire system during the discussion. The teacher will emphasize that all these parts are integrated and balanced, and the students will follow this aspect during their conversation.
Outcome: They produce detailed observation notes as well as better insights into system dynamics and balance.
practicals.title: Observing Variability in an Interactive Simulation
practicals.aim: To understand how variability affects a system of interest by changing variables in an interactive simulation and observing the system’s response.

practicals.label: Activity 1.04
practicals.bookText:
Simulation Game
**Objective:** To experience managing a system and making decisions to keep it functional.
**Required Material:** Computers or tablets with internet access, city simulation game (e.g., SimCity).
**Activity Type:** Pair (Group of two students)
**Activity Tasks Detail:** Begin with an introduction to the simulation game, explaining its objectives and mechanics. Students will then play the game in pairs, making strategic decisions to manage their city. After gameplay, a debriefing session will allow students to discuss their experiences, challenges, and strategies. The teacher will link these experiences to system management concepts discussed in class.
**Output:** Hands-on gameplay experience and reflection on system management challenges and strategies.
procedure: Work in pairs.
Begin with an introduction to the simulation game, including its objectives and mechanics.
Play the game with your partner, making strategic decisions to manage the city.
After gameplay, discuss your experiences, challenges, and strategies.
Relate the gameplay experience to system management concepts discussed in class.
practicals.aim: To experience managing a system and making decisions to keep it functional.

viva.question: What is a simulation game?
viva.answer: A game that models a real or imagined system for users to interact with.

viva.question: What is the objective of this activity?
viva.answer: To practise managing a system and making decisions to keep it functional.

viva.question: What does system management involve in the game?
viva.answer: Making decisions and using resources to manage the city.

viva.question: Why do students play in pairs?
viva.answer: To discuss choices and work together on city management.

viva.question: What is a debriefing session?
viva.answer: A discussion after gameplay about experiences, challenges, and strategies.

practicals.title: Managing a City with a Simulation Game
precautions: Use the computer or tablet carefully and keep it on a stable surface.
Use only the assigned simulation game and follow the teacher’s instructions.
Make decisions together with your partner and take turns using the device.
Do not share personal information while using an online game.
practicals.result: The city simulation provided hands-on experience in managing a system. We discussed the challenges and strategies involved in keeping the city functional.

practicals.label: Activity 1.05
practicals.bookText:
The Journey of Data
**Objectives:** Students will discover how computer components work together to process and display data.
**Required Material:** Markers, index cards, and a flowchart template are required.
**Pair-based activity:** Tasks. Begin with an introduction to data processing in computers. Students will work in pairs to create a flowchart illustrating the data stream from input to output. Each pair will present their flowcharts and participate in a class discussion to highlight key points.
**Output:** Improved presentation and debating skills, as well as thorough flowcharts depicting the data path.
procedure: Begin with an introduction to data processing in computers.
Work in pairs to create a flowchart illustrating the data stream from input to output.
Present the flowchart to the class.
Participate in a class discussion to highlight key points.
practicals.aim: To show how computer components work together as data moves from input to output.

viva.question: What is data processing?
viva.answer: It is the process of transforming input data into useful information.

viva.question: What is the first stage in the data stream shown in your flowchart?
viva.answer: Input.

viva.question: What happens during processing?
viva.answer: The computer works on the input data according to instructions.

viva.question: What is output?
viva.answer: The information produced by the computer after processing.

viva.question: What does an arrow in a flowchart show?
viva.answer: The direction or sequence of the flow.

practicals.diagram: Draw a flowchart with three labelled boxes—Input, Processing, and Output—joined by arrows in that order.
practicals.title: The Journey of Data
precautions: Write each flowchart label clearly.
Draw arrows to show the correct direction from input to output.
Keep the flowchart neat and easy to follow.
Listen respectfully to other pairs during presentations and discussion.
practicals.result: A flowchart was created to show the path of data from input through processing to output. The activity also helped develop presentation and discussion skills.

practicals.label: Activity 1.06
practicals.bookText:
Exploring Computer Components
**Objective:** Students will learn about the different components of a computer and their functions.
**Required Material:** Physical computer parts (CPU, RAM, etc.), diagrams of computer systems, worksheets for labeling and note-taking.
**Activity Type:** Group (Small groups of 3-4 students)
**Activity Tasks Detail:** The teacher will start with an overview of key computer components. Students will then work in small groups identifying and labeling computer parts using worksheets. Groups will present their findings in a session, followed by a Q&A where the teacher clarifies any misunderstandings.
**Output:** Labeled worksheets, enhanced presentation skills, and a deeper understanding of computer components.
procedure: Listen to the teacher’s overview of key computer components.
Work in a small group to identify the physical computer parts.
Use the diagrams of computer systems to identify and label the computer parts on the worksheet.
Present the group’s findings to the class.
Take part in the question-and-answer session and clarify any misunderstandings.
practicals.aim: To identify different computer components and learn their functions.

viva.question: What is the CPU?
viva.answer: The CPU processes instructions and controls the operations of the computer.

viva.question: What is RAM used for?
viva.answer: RAM temporarily stores data and instructions that the CPU is currently using.

viva.question: What is a computer component?
viva.answer: A computer component is a hardware part that performs a function in a computer system.

viva.question: What is the function of a monitor?
viva.answer: A monitor displays visual output from the computer.

viva.question: Name one input device.
viva.answer: A keyboard is an input device.

apparatus: Physical computer parts, including the CPU and RAM
practicals.diagram: Draw a computer system and label the CPU, RAM, monitor, keyboard, and mouse.
practicals.title: Identifying Computer Components
precautions: Handle physical computer parts carefully and by their edges.
Do not touch electrical contacts or circuit components unnecessarily.
Do not connect or disconnect computer parts while the computer is powered on.
Keep food and liquids away from the computer parts and worksheets.
practicals.result: The computer components were identified and labelled, and their functions were discussed. The group presented its findings.

practicals.label: Activity 1.08
practicals.bookText:
Computing Systems Around Us
**Activity Tasks Detail:** Start with an introduction on computing systems. Students will then research and list various computing systems they use daily, completing a worksheet. In a group sharing session, students will discuss their findings. The class will engage in a discussion to highlight key points, and students will begin preparing a short presentation on a computing system for the next class.
**Output:** Completed worksheets, group insights, and a short presentation on a chosen computing system.
Tidbits
**Internet Systems**
1. When you send an email or browse the internet, data travels through cables and airwaves across the world in just seconds. It's like sending a letter that gets delivered instantly, regardless of distance!
2. The internet is one of the largest man-made systems ever created. It's a vast network of interconnected computers that communicate with each other to share information, much like how our brain's neurons communicate. When you send a message, it travels through multiple networks before reaching its destination, all within seconds.
3. Data on the internet travels at nearly the speed of light! When you send a message or browse a website, your data can cross continents almost instantaneously.
4. There are over 1.5 billion websites on the internet today, and more than 4 billion people are connected to the internet globally. That's more than half of the world's population!
SUMMARY
- A system is a collection of parts that work together to achieve a common goal.
- A system is described by its objective, components, communication among components and environment in which it works.
- Components are the building blocks of any system. Each component plays a specific role and contributes to the overall functionality of the system.
- The environment of a system includes everything external to the system that interacts with it. It consists of all external factors that affect system's operation.
- Systems can be broadly categorized into two types, namely natural and artificial systems.
- Natural systems are those that exist in nature and operate independently of human involvement.
- Artificial systems are designed and constructed by humans.
- Social systems are organized structures created by humans to manage social relationships, governance, and community activities.
- Computer science is the study of how computers work. It looks at what computers can do and what limitations they have.
- A computer is a complex system designed to process data and perform tasks according to a set of instructions.
- The Von Neumann architecture involves several key steps for a CPU to execute instructions, including fetching, decoding, executing, and storing.
- System software is the basic software that helps a computer run and manage its hardware and software resources.
- Application software is the software designed to help users perform specific tasks or activities.
practicals.title: Computing Systems Around Us
practicals.aim: To identify computing systems used in daily life, record how their components work together, share findings, and begin a short presentation on one system.
